transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because... I just don't care about anything anymore. Like, nothing at all. I used to do all this stuff, like my art classes and board-game nights. We used to play this one game with little wooden pieces, and my friend Sarah always had to be the blue ones. She actually moved to Oregon recently. I don't know why anyone would want to move there, it rains constantly. Rain always makes my car smell weird, kind of like wet dog, even though I don't even own a dog. My neighbor has a beagle that never stops howling, though, especially when the mail carrier comes... 

But anyway, I don't even care about going hiking anymore, or trying to get back on my soccer team. I just... I just sit in my room while everything slips away. It's just me in that room. The window has this really bad draft, but I don't really do anything about it.
Have you ever had a distinct period when your mood was unusually high or unusually irritable?

Unusually high? Um... no. No, I don't think I've ever felt like that. I'm just... always down. Or tired. I mean, my sister gets really hyper sometimes, but she drinks like four of those energy drinks every single day. The ones in the bright green cans? I don't know how she affords them, honestly, they're like four dollars at the gas station on the corner. The guy who works at that gas station always looks at me funny, though. He has this huge clock behind the counter that ticks so loud, it echoes in the whole store, and I just stare at the second hand going around and around... I hate clocks that tick. 

But, um... no. I don't get high moods. Just heavy.
Have you ever had a period when you felt back to your usual self for at least two months?

Back to my usual self? No... no, I haven't. It's just been this same heavy feeling for... well, it started shortly after the divorce. That was about a year and eleven months ago now. My ex-husband, he actually took the microwave when he left. Can you believe that? Who takes a microwave? It was one of those really old ones, too, the kind with the dial instead of the buttons. I had to go to Target to buy a new one, and the parking lot there is always an absolute nightmare. People just don't know how to drive, especially when they're pushing those red carts around. I saw a lady back right into a shopping cart corral once, and she just drove off like nothing happened. The cart corral was totally dented, just bent out of shape... 

But yeah, no. I haven't felt normal for almost two years. Just... stuck.
During this nearly two-year period, has there been a stretch of at least two weeks when your depression was noticeably worse than usual?

Yeah, I mean... worse than usual? It's all just bad. Most of the time since this whole thing took over, I haven't just been, you know, scared of the guy at the gas station or confused by things... I've been so deeply depressed. Like, barely interested in anything. I just feel like my life is already over. It's like being buried alive, but you still have to breathe. Breathing is actually really hard sometimes, especially when it's humid out. I used to have this dehumidifier in my old apartment, it was this big gray box that sounded like a jet engine taking off. My landlord there was terrible, he never fixed anything. He wore these awful Hawaiian shirts every single day, even in December. I don't know where you even buy Hawaiian shirts in the winter. Maybe online? I don't really shop online anymore, the boxes just pile up by the door and I don't have the energy to break them down for recycling. The recycling truck comes on Thursdays, and it's so loud it shakes the whole street... but yeah, mostly I'm just deeply, deeply depressed all the time. Like there's no point to anything.
How has your sleep been during this period?

Sleep? Um... it's terrible. I just... I lie awake for hours, mostly. I have to keep checking the door, making sure it's locked, and I just listen to every little sound in the house. The pipes in my building make this awful groaning noise, like someone is trapped inside them. It reminds me of this horror movie I watched when I was a teenager, with my friend Sarah. Sarah had this huge golden retriever that shed everywhere, her mom was constantly vacuuming. She had one of those really expensive vacuums, a Dyson, I think? The yellow ones. I always wanted a vacuum like that, but they cost like five hundred dollars. Who spends that much on a vacuum? Anyway, when I finally do fall asleep, it doesn't last. I always wake up way before dawn, just... shaking. Completely shaking. And I can't get back to sleep after that, no matter what I do. I can't get back under the covers, I just sit there. So yeah, I don't sleep much at all.
Have you had thoughts about killing yourself or ending your life?

Thoughts about ending it... yeah. I do. I just keep having these thoughts that I don't want to wake up anymore. Waking up is the hardest part of the day. I have these heavy curtains in my bedroom to block the sun, I bought them at Bed Bath & Beyond right before they went out of business. It was actually really sad, seeing all those huge yellow liquidation signs in the windows. I used to love going in there just to smell the candles. They had this one, 'Autumn Wreath' I think it was called, that smelled exactly like my grandmother's house at Thanksgiving. She used to make this incredible cranberry sauce from scratch, not the jelly stuff that keeps the shape of the tin. I hate the canned stuff, it wiggles too much on the plate, it just looks wrong. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh. Yeah, my friend came over the other day, and when she found me, I guess I had been saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. Just saying it over and over to the room. I didn't even realize I was talking out loud until she touched my shoulder. She brought me some soup, but I just... I couldn't eat it. I can't keep doing this.
Has this depressed mood been present more days than not for at least two full years?

Two years? Um... no, not quite that long. It really became constant, like, every single day constant, around the summer after it all started. So it's been about... maybe a year and four months of just this heavy, dark feeling all the time. That summer was so hot, too. The AC in my car broke right in July, and the mechanic said it would cost eight hundred dollars to fix. Eight hundred dollars! I drove around with the windows down, but the wind just messes up your hair and makes everything loud. I remember driving past this huge field of sunflowers on the way to the grocery store. They all looked so bright and yellow, but they were all facing the exact same way, like an army. It was actually kind of creepy. Sunflowers are supposed to be happy, right? But they just looked like they were plotting something. I bought some sunflower seeds once to plant in a pot on my balcony, but a squirrel dug them all up before they could even sprout. Squirrels are so bold now, they just stare right at you. But yeah, about a year and four months of feeling like this.
